# What does this PR do?

Stops MTP speculative decoding from mixing requests in the draft step when the MTP head has no draft KV plane. Each request's draft now sees only its own position, as a sequence of one token. Attention layers hand core attention those sequences as an ordinary sbhd batch, and recurrent layers take one step per sequence from a zero state, so no backend needs varlen support or host syncs for them.

## The bug

Without a draft KV plane, the dynamic engine drafts through `LanguageModule.compute_mtp_single_step` -> `MultiTokenPredictionLayer.forward_single_position` with no inference context. The controller lays the N active requests along the sequence dimension: token ids `[1, N]`, hidden states `[N, 1, H]` (split across TP ranks under sequence parallelism). The MTP layer saw one N-token sequence:

- Its causal attention let request j attend to requests 0..j-1.
- A recurrent layer in a hybrid head (Mamba, Gated Delta Product, KDA, GDN2) ran its convolution and scan across requests.

On `main`, replacing every other request moves the last request's draft logits already at the first draft depth, where the regression test stops (H100 results below). Greedy outputs are unaffected because drafts are verified. The acceptance rate drops, and it depends on which requests share the batch.

This path runs whenever the draft KV plane is off. `MTPContextMixin.should_enable_mtp_kv_cache` reserves the plane only for a repeated head (`mtp_use_repeated_layer=True`), and for a hybrid head only with exactly one attention layer and otherwise only MLP and MoE layers. MLA heads never get one. Heads with one layer per depth, as in DeepSeek-V3 checkpoints, always draft this way.

## Root cause and fix

Without a context, the draft step has no history to attend over. Training's MTP attends within each sequence, and the draft KV plane gives every request its own attention metadata. The context-free step had no sequence boundaries at all.

`forward_single_position` now passes the MTP layer `PackedSeqParams.single_token_sequences(N)` when it has no context: THD params with `cu_seqlens = [0, 1, ..., N]`, `max_seqlen = 1` and a precomputed `seq_idx`, one sequence per row. The token layout does not change, so sequence parallelism, MoE and expert-parallel padding rows, and the hidden-state chain across depths keep working. Forwards with a context are unchanged: the draft KV plane, the commit pass, and the EP dummy forward.

`PackedSeqParams.has_single_token_sequences()` names the case. Two contracts run it, one for each kind of sequence mixer:

- **Attention** (`Attention._runs_tokens_as_batch`, used by `Attention` and `MultiLatentAttention`). Only core attention needs the boundaries, so that each query sees its own key alone. The projections, norms and rotary embeddings work per token, so they run the tokens `[t, 1, ...]` as one unpacked sequence, as for any input; RoPE rotates a query and its only key by the same angle, which leaves their product unchanged. Core attention then gets the sbhd batch `[1, t, ...]` of length-1 sequences and no pack, so TE, local, Kitchen or any other core attention runs it without THD support. DSA keeps the pack, because its indexer reads the layer input, which sequence parallelism splits along the tokens.
- **Recurrent mixers** (`megatron.core.ssm.ssm_inference.steps_from_zero_state`). In inference, every token starts a recurrence of its own: the short conv sees the token alone and the recurrence takes one step from a zero state, which it neither reads nor stores. Each mixer runs that step on all tokens at once with its own projection, conv and gate code, through kernels that need no varlen metadata and keep no state per sequence. The step kernels of GDP, KDA and GDN2 have no backward, hence inference only.

| Mixer (hybrid symbol) | How a single-token pack runs |
|---|---|
| GQA/MHA attention (`*`), any core attention | Unpacked projections, then core attention on the sbhd batch `[1, t]` |
| MLA (`+`) | Same. RoPE runs on the unpacked sequence, as on `main`, instead of the vectorized THD RoPE; V is not padded |
| DSA over GQA (`*` with the DSA-GQA spec) | Same; its indexer gets the layer input as the same batch (DSA over GQA rules out sequence parallelism) |
| DSA over MLA (`D`) | Keeps the pack and takes DSA's packed path. The indexer now passes `max_seqlen` to its packed RoPE, which removes the path's only host sync |
| DSv4 CSA / HCA / window (`C`, `H`, `W`) | DSv4 runs at TP 1, so nothing splits its tokens: the whole layer runs on the batch `[1, t, h]`. Its packed path needs the cuDNN backend |
| Mamba (`M`) | The conv runs over each token as a row `[t, d, 1]`, with pip `causal_conv1d` or the `F.conv1d` fallback; the chunked scan runs on `[1, t]` and restarts at every token through `seq_idx`, keeping `ceil(t / chunk_size)` chunk states as on `main` |
| Gated Delta Product (`M`, GDP spec) | `ssm_decode` without state caches: the training path's conv (pip `causal_conv1d_fn` or its fallback) over each token, then the in-tree fused recurrence from a zero state. The decode CUDA graphs run the forked `causal_conv1d_update` instead |
| KDA (`K`) | KDA's own projection code (`_input_projections`), its conv and gate code on the batch of length-1 sequences (FLA conv or the fallback; the packed-input conv padding is not needed), then one step of FLA's `fused_recurrent_kda` |
| GDN2 (`G` with `gdn2`) | GDN2's own conv and gate code on the batch, then one step of FLA's `fused_recurrent_gdn2`, or the torch backend's kernel when `gdn_kernel_backend="torch"` |
| GDN (`G`) | Unchanged: GDN rejects inference without a context before it reads the pack |
| MLP (`-`), MoE (`E`) | Per token; MoE reads only the pack's CP fields, which it leaves unset |

Mamba's unfused (non-memory-efficient) path still rejects packed training input, as on `main`: it takes packed input only as sequences of one token each in inference, at CP 1. Packed training keeps running the memory-efficient path, which also lays packed sequences out for context parallelism.

Hot-path cost per draft depth, eager: one `arange` of N+1 int32 for the pack. Attention and MLA run the projections and RoPE `main` ran. Mamba copies its conv input once, as `main` did. GDP, KDA and GDN2 launch fewer kernels than their chunked scans.

### Why not the other options

- **Requests along the batch dimension** (`[1, N, H]`). Sequence parallelism splits the sequence dimension across TP ranks, and every SP linear gathers and scatters along it. A length-1 sequence cannot be split, so the rows stay on the sequence dimension, and attention swaps them onto the batch dimension only after the projections have gathered them.
- **Each mixer's general THD path.** It is correct, but GDP, KDA and GDN2 then host-sync (FLA's varlen chunk indices) and keep a chunk state per sequence, MLA pads V and runs the THD RoPE, and DSA over GQA and DSv4 (without cuDNN) reject packing.
- **A draft KV plane for every head.** That is a design question, not a fix. Each MTP depth after the first would need history built from tokens that are still drafts.

Replacing every other request leaves the last request's draft logits bit-identical. Each request also matches, within 2% of the largest logit, its own draft run alone through the ordinary unpacked path, which shares no code with the single-token paths. The cached-latent MLA case skips until the MLA draft fix below is present. On `main` the bit-identity check fails at depth 0.

The replay matches the eager draft; a replay with the other requests replaced changes every replaced request's drafts and leaves the last request's bit-identical.

## Follow-ups: KDA MTP heads, FLA's `g` reads, the draft-plane predicate

Review findings on KDA and GDN2 heads, fixed in two commits (26cdb2776 and the one after it). H100 results are at the end of this section.

- **A head with KDA and one attention layer crashed at the first step.** `should_enable_mtp_kv_cache` counted only Mamba and GDN as recurrent, so a repeated head such as `K*` (pattern `M*/K*` or `*-/K*`) got the draft KV plane. The controller then handed the dynamic context to the head's KDA layer, which asserts static batching. Such a head now drafts without a context, on this PR's single-token path.
- **The predicate is an allowlist now.** It listed the mixers that must not get the plane, so the next one missed would fail as KDA did. A hybrid head gets the plane only with exactly one attention layer that can use it (`*`, `D` or `+`) and otherwise only MLP and MoE layers. Every other mixer drafts without a context: Mamba, GDN, KDA, and DSv4 attention (`C`, `H`, `W`), which rejects every inference context. A head such as `*C` used to get the plane and then fail DSv4's assertion; it now drafts on the single-token path, which DSv4 supports.
- **KDA in the main decoder is rejected when the engine is built.** `KimiDeltaAttention` rejects every inference context, so a decoder with KDA layers used to fail at its first forward. `MambaInferenceStateConfig.from_model` now raises `NotImplementedError` for it, as it already does for GDN2. An MTP head may still hold KDA layers, since it drafts without a context.
- **FLA's recurrent KDA and GDN2 kernels read past `g` when the key head dim is not a power of two.** FLA 0.5.1 loads each (token, head) row of `g` in `fused_recurrent_kda` and `fused_recurrent_gdn2` `next_power_of_2(K)` wide without a mask (`fla/ops/kda/fused_recurrent.py:158`, `fla/ops/gdn2/fused_recurrent.py:177`). For K = 96, 160, 192, ..., the last row reads BK − K elements past the end of `g`, and a NaN there makes that head's draft NaN. This PR reaches both kernels. FLA 0.6.0 masks both loads, so this PR is now stacked on the FLA bump (#8861, `fix/fla-core-g-overrun`) instead of padding around the library bug. The `g` pad of 26cdb2776, which covered KDA only and copied `g` at every draft depth, is gone.

Tests (1 GPU each, except where noted):

- `TestMtpKvCacheGating` in `test_dynamic_context_mtp_kv_cache.py`: `K*`, `*K` and `*C` heads get no draft KV plane, and `*-` and `E*` heads do. Before 26cdb2776, `K*` and `*K` get one; before the allowlist, `*C` does.
- `test_kda_single_token_sequences_read_only_g` in `test_kda.py` (one- and two-stage gates) and `test_gdn2_single_token_sequences_read_only_g` in `test_gated_delta_net2.py`, both at a key head dim of 96. Each runs a single-token pack with `g` handed on as a view at the start of a NaN-filled buffer. Every output must be finite and match the token's run alone. They pass with any fix of the read and fail on FLA 0.5.1, where the last (token, head) row is NaN. Both also pass under compute-sanitizer memcheck with `PYTORCH_NO_CUDA_MEMORY_CACHING=1`, with no memcheck errors.
- `test_mamba_inference_state_config_rejects_kda_in_decoder` in `test_inference_config.py` (CPU): decoders with KDA layers raise when the engine is built. Before this commit, they don't. Checked on CPU.

On H100 in the CI image (`mcore_ci_dev:main`, 2026-11-02), at this head, with #8861's `uv.lock` change applied in the container (FLA 0.6.0, for this PR and its base):
- The regression tests pass: 45 cases on 1 GPU, including the three tests above, and 20 on 2 GPUs (`TestMTPDraftStepRequestIsolation`, with the same 3 skips).
- On the stacked base (#8861), the 2-GPU test fails in 20 cases at depth 0 ("the other requests moved the last one's drafts"). The 1-GPU tests only fail at import there: `test_kda.py` and `test_gated_delta_net2.py` import `followed_by_nan`, a test helper this PR adds, and that collection error stops the 1-GPU run before any case. So this run does not show the KDA and GDN2 findings on the base. The step 3 GPU repros did, on `main` on H100: R01-F2 (4 of 4 cases: the context reserves the draft KV plane for a `K*` or `*K` head and hands the dynamic context to KDA, which raises) and R01-F3 (8 of 8 kernel cases: FLA 0.5.1's `fused_recurrent_kda` puts NaN in the output at K = 96 and 192 with NaN after `g`).
- The neighbors pass: `TestMTPCudaGraphInference` (28 cases, 2 GPUs), `test_mamba_mixer.py` (22, at 8 GPUs) and `test_kda_packed_matches_unpacked_cp1` (2).
- Under compute-sanitizer memcheck there are no memcheck errors, and 34 cases on 1 GPU and 13 on 2 GPUs pass. 18 cases that capture a CUDA graph fail at capture: with the caching allocator off, as this memcheck run sets it, the capture calls `cuMemAlloc`, which a capturing stream does not permit. So those graphed cases have not run under memcheck.

## Interaction with other open PRs

- n12 ([#8709](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/8709), `fix/n12-inference-all-gather-barrier`) moves KDA's input projections into the same `_input_projections` helper this PR adds and lets `in_proj` and `beta_proj` share one all-gather there. KDA's single-token step calls that helper, so it inherits the shared all-gather. Merging the two conflicts in `kda.py` only, in the imports and around the helper; whichever lands second keeps n12's version of the helper and both imports. `gated_delta_product.py` merges cleanly.
- n7 ([#8703](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/8703), `fix/n7-mla-mtp-draft`, "[Inference][MLA][MTP] Let latent-caching MLA layers run MTP draft steps without an inference context"): without it, MLA heads with cached latents cannot draft at all. With both, an MLA draft step takes MLA's unabsorbed path on the unpacked sequence, then core attention on the batch. The two conflict only in the parametrize lists of `TestMtpKvCacheGating` (keep both sides' cases); n7's MLA case still holds, since n7 turns the plane off for MLA configs before the layer check. Whichever lands second removes the skip of the cached-latent MLA case.
- #8570 (d5) rejects DSA with dynamic-batching MLA, so DSA heads do not draft in the engine. This PR still keeps DSA's packed path free of host syncs.
- n10 ([#8706](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/8706), `fix/n10-gdp-conv-stride`) aligns GDP's conv input; it merges cleanly with the conv helper this PR factors out of `_prepare_qkv`.
- #8861 (`fix/fla-core-g-overrun`, the FLA 0.6.0 bump): this PR is stacked on it. Merge order: #8861 first, with its regenerated `uv.lock`, then this PR, so that KDA and GDN2 drafts never run on an FLA that reads past `g`. The two touch different files.
- #8883 (`fix/kda-fla-deterministic`) conflicts with this PR in `test_ssm_kernels.py` only, as it did before these follow-ups.
- #8568 (d6) and #8569 (S10) change Mamba decode, and n9 ([#8705](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/8705), `fix/n9-mtp-norm-sequence-parallel`) adds a test in `TestMultiTokenPredictionLayer`. All merge cleanly, as do #8563 (d3+S6), #8565 (S2) and S8.

## Issue tracking

Linked issue: none; the regression test reproduces the bug.

## Code provenance

No code was copied from other repositories.

## Contribution process

### Pre-checks

- [x] I have added relevant unit tests
- [ ] I have added relevant functional tests
- [x] If this PR adds or changes a GPU kernel (Triton, `jit_fuser`/`torch.compile`, CUDA extension, TE or external-library dispatch, or a scatter/index accumulation), I have added or updated its bit-exact determinism test and registered it in `tests/unit_tests/determinism/kernels/manifest.py` (new dispatch of the stateless GDP recurrence, FLA's recurrent KDA/GDN2 kernels and Mamba's single-token unfused path is replayed in `test_ssm_kernels.py`; the attention-side changes need the `determinism-exempt` label)
- [x] I have added proper typing to my code [Typing guidelines](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html)
- [ ] I have added relevant documentation
- [x] I have run the [autoformatter.sh](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/main/tools/autoformat.sh) on my PR

## Follow-ups: KDA MTP heads, FLA's `g` reads, the draft-plane predicate

Review findings on KDA and GDN2 heads, fixed in two commits (26cdb2776 and the one after it). H100 results are at the end of this section.

- **A head with KDA and one attention layer crashed at the first step.** `should_enable_mtp_kv_cache` counted only Mamba and GDN as recurrent, so a repeated head such as `K*` (pattern `M*/K*` or `*-/K*`) got the draft KV plane. The controller then handed the dynamic context to the head's KDA layer, which asserts static batching. Such a head now drafts without a context, on this PR's single-token path.
- **The predicate is an allowlist now.** It listed the mixers that must not get the plane, so the next one missed would fail as KDA did. A hybrid head gets the plane only with exactly one attention layer that can use it (`*`, `D` or `+`) and otherwise only MLP and MoE layers. Every other mixer drafts without a context: Mamba, GDN, KDA, and DSv4 attention (`C`, `H`, `W`), which rejects every inference context. A head such as `*C` used to get the plane and then fail DSv4's assertion; it now drafts on the single-token path, which DSv4 supports.
- **KDA in the main decoder is rejected when the engine is built.** `KimiDeltaAttention` rejects every inference context, so a decoder with KDA layers used to fail at its first forward. `MambaInferenceStateConfig.from_model` now raises `NotImplementedError` for it, as it already does for GDN2. +"""The FLA context-parallel kernels the GDP chunkwise CP backend launches directly.
+
+``megatron/core/ssm/context_parallel/gdp.py`` launches FLA's CP summary kernels and its CP merge
+kernel itself, outside FLA's wrappers, for both BLH (several sequences per launch) and varlen
+boundary fragments. Each launch must replay bit-exactly and meet the contract chunkwise CP builds
+on, checked against a computation that does not go through those launches:
+
+- forward summary ``[h_local | M]``: a fragment started from a state ``h_in`` ends at
+  ``M @ h_in + h_local``. FLA's chunk scan (``chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_h``) gives ``h_local``
+  from a zero state, and ``M @ h_in`` from ``h_in`` with zero values;
+- backward summary ``[dh_local | dM]``: a gradient ``dh_out`` at the fragment's end reaches its
+  start as ``dM @ dh_out + dh_local``. FLA's backward chunk scan
+  (``chunk_gated_delta_rule_bwd_dhu``) gives ``dh_local`` with no gradient at the end, and
+  ``dM @ dh_out`` from ``dh_out`` alone;
+- merge: the summaries compose from a zero state in rank order (forward) or in reverse rank order
+  (backward), recomputed here in FP64.
+
+The two parts of each summary are checked separately, so that neither can hide behind the other.

+        chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_h,
+    )
+    from fla.ops.utils import chunk_local_cumsum
+    from fla.ops.utils.constant import RCP_LN2

+    HAVE_FLA = True
+except ImportError:
+    HAVE_FLA = False

+    pytest.mark.skipif(not torch.cuda.is_available(), reason="CUDA is unavailable"),
+    pytest.mark.skipif(not HAVE_FLA, reason="FLA is not installed"),
+]

+    the CP kernels gdp.py launches) is an error, not a skip."""

+        w=beta * k.repeat_interleave(VALUE_HEADS // KEY_HEADS, dim=2),
+        u=torch.randn(*shape, VALUE_HEADS, VALUE_DIM, device="cuda"),
+        do=torch.randn(*shape, VALUE_HEADS, VALUE_DIM, device="cuda"),
+        dv=torch.randn(*shape, VALUE_HEADS, VALUE_DIM, device="cuda"),

+"""FLA's fused recurrent KDA and GDN2 kernels must read only the gate rows they are given.
+
+The kernels tile the head dim K to BK = next_power_of_2(K) and read each (token, head) row of the
+per-channel gate ``g`` with stride K. Before FLA 0.6.0 that load had no mask, so the last row read
+BK - K elements past the end of ``g``, and a NaN pattern there turned that head's output NaN.
+Megatron runs these kernels on packed single-token sequences, and KDA and GDN2 accept head dims
+that are not a power of two (96, 160, 192, ...).
+
+Each case runs one step from a zero state, whose output does not depend on the gate, with ``g`` a
+contiguous view at the start of a NaN-filled buffer.
+"""
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+import torch.nn.functional as F
+
+try:
+    from fla.ops.gdn2.fused_recurrent import fused_recurrent_gdn2
+    from fla.ops.kda import fused_recurrent_kda
+
+    HAVE_FLA = True
+except ImportError:
+    HAVE_FLA = False
+
+pytestmark = [
+    pytest.mark.skipif(not HAVE_FLA, reason="FLA is not installed"),
+    pytest.mark.skipif(not torch.cuda.is_available(), reason="needs a CUDA GPU"),
+]
+
+NUM_TOKENS, NUM_HEADS = 6, 4
+
+
+def _inputs(head_dim):
+    """BF16 [N, 1, H, K] q/k/v, as single-token sequences pass them, and their generator."""
+    gen = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(head_dim)
+
+    def randn(*size):
+        return torch.randn(*size, generator=gen, device="cuda")
+
+    shape = (NUM_TOKENS, 1, NUM_HEADS, head_dim)
+    q, k, v = (randn(*shape).bfloat16() for _ in range(3))
+    return q, k, v, randn
+
+
+def _followed_by_nan(values):
+    """``values`` as a contiguous view at the start of a NaN-filled buffer."""
+    buffer = torch.full(
+        (values.numel() + 1024,), float("nan"), dtype=values.dtype, device=values.device
+    )
+    buffer[: values.numel()] = values.flatten()
+    return buffer[: values.numel()].view(values.shape)
+
+
+def _one_step(q, k, value, l2norm):
+    """Output of one step from a zero state: ``value * (q . k) / sqrt(K)``, in FP32."""
+    q, k = q.float(), k.float()
+    if l2norm:
+        q = q / torch.sqrt((q * q).sum(-1, keepdim=True) + 1e-6)
+        k = k / torch.sqrt((k * k).sum(-1, keepdim=True) + 1e-6)
+    return value * (q * k).sum(-1, keepdim=True) * q.shape[-1] ** -0.5
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("lower_bound", [-5.0, None])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("l2norm", [False, True])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("head_dim", [64, 96, 192])
+def test_fused_recurrent_kda_reads_only_g(head_dim, l2norm, lower_bound):
+    q, k, v, randn = _inputs(head_dim)
+    beta = torch.sigmoid(randn(NUM_TOKENS, 1, NUM_HEADS))
+    out, _ = fused_recurrent_kda(
+        q,
+        k,
+        v,
+        _followed_by_nan(randn(*q.shape).bfloat16()),
+        beta,
+        A_log=randn(NUM_HEADS),
+        dt_bias=randn(NUM_HEADS * head_dim),
+        use_qk_l2norm_in_kernel=l2norm,
+        use_gate_in_kernel=True,
+        lower_bound=lower_bound,
+    )
+    expected = _one_step(q, k, beta[..., None] * v.float(), l2norm)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(out.float(), expected, atol=5e-2, rtol=2e-2)
+
+

+# from the raw gate features.
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("gate_in_kernel", [False, True])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("l2norm", [False, True])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("head_dim", [64, 96, 192])
+def test_fused_recurrent_gdn2_reads_only_g(head_dim, l2norm, gate_in_kernel):

+    out, _ = fused_recurrent_gdn2(
+        q,
+        k,
+        v,
+        _followed_by_nan(g),
+        erase,
+        write,
+        use_qk_l2norm_in_kernel=l2norm,
+        use_gate_in_kernel=gate_in_kernel,
+        **gate,
+    )
+    expected = _one_step(q, k, write.float() * v.float(), l2norm)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(out.float(), expected, atol=5e-2, rtol=2e-2)

+            position_embedding_type="none",
+        )
+        return model.cuda().eval()
+
+    def _inputs(self, seed):
+        """Per-request draft inputs: base hidden state, and the next token at every depth."""
+        generator = torch.Generator().manual_seed(seed)
+        hidden = torch.randn(self.NUM_REQUESTS, 1, self.HIDDEN_SIZE, generator=generator)
+        tokens = torch.randint(
+            0, self.VOCAB_SIZE, (self.MTP_DEPTHS, self.NUM_REQUESTS), generator=generator
+        )
+        return hidden.to("cuda", torch.bfloat16), tokens.cuda()
+
+    def _inputs_with_others_replaced(self):
+        """Two batches that share only their last request."""
+        hidden, tokens = self._inputs(seed=1)
+        other_hidden, other_tokens = self._inputs(seed=2)
+        last = self.NUM_REQUESTS - 1
+        other_hidden[last], other_tokens[:, last] = hidden[last], tokens[:, last]
+        return (hidden, tokens), (other_hidden, other_tokens)
+
+    def _draft(self, model, hidden, tokens):
+        """Run the draft depths on one row per request, as the MTP controller does.
+
+        Pads the rows to a multiple of TP and scatters them for sequence parallelism. Returns
+        each depth's logits for the real rows, [num_requests, vocab].
+        """
+        num_requests = hidden.size(0)
+        tp_group = get_tensor_model_parallel_group()
+        tp = get_pg_size(tp_group)
+        pad = -num_requests % tp
+        hidden = torch.nn.functional.pad(hidden, (0, 0, 0, 0, 0, pad))
+        tokens = torch.nn.functional.pad(tokens, (0, pad))
+        positions = torch.arange(num_requests + pad, device="cuda").unsqueeze(0)
+        if model.config.sequence_parallel:
+            hidden = scatter_to_sequence_parallel_region(hidden, group=tp_group)
+        logits_per_depth = []
+        for depth in range(self.MTP_DEPTHS):
+            hidden, logits = model.compute_mtp_single_step(
+                hidden_states=hidden,
+                next_token_ids=tokens[depth : depth + 1],
+                position_ids=positions + depth,
+                depth=depth,
+            )
+            logits_per_depth.append(logits[:num_requests, 0].float())
+        return logits_per_depth
+
+    def _draft_alone(self, model, hidden, tokens, monkeypatch):
+        """Draft each request alone, as the one real token of an ordinary unpacked sequence.
+
+        The reference is independent of how a batch runs single-token sequences: the draft step
+        gets no packing, so every layer takes its ordinary path, where one request (followed by
+        TP padding) cannot see another. Returns each request's drafts, as `_draft` does.
+        """
+        with monkeypatch.context() as patch:
+            patch.setattr(
+                PackedSeqParams,
+                "single_token_sequences",
+                staticmethod(lambda *args, **kwargs: None),
+                raising=False,
+            )
+            return [
+                self._draft(model, hidden[i : i + 1], tokens[:, i : i + 1])
+                for i in range(hidden.size(0))
+            ]
+
+    def _assert_last_request_unmoved(self, batched, replaced):
+        last = self.NUM_REQUESTS - 1
+        for depth in range(self.MTP_DEPTHS):
+            torch.testing.assert_close(
+                replaced[depth][last],
+                batched[depth][last],
+                rtol=0,
+                atol=0,
+                msg=lambda m: f"depth {depth}: the other requests moved the last one's drafts\n{m}",
+            )
+
+    @pytest.mark.parametrize("tp", [1, 2])
+    @pytest.mark.parametrize(
+        "model_type", ["gpt", "mla", "mla_cached_latents", "mamba", "gdp", "kda", "gdn2", "dsa_gqa"]
+    )
+    def test_draft_logits_do_not_depend_on_other_requests(self, model_type, tp, monkeypatch):
+        if Utils.world_size < tp:
+            pytest.skip(f"TP={tp} requires at least {tp} ranks")
+        if model_type == "dsa_gqa" and tp > 1:
+            pytest.skip("DSA over GQA does not support sequence parallelism")
+        model = self._build_model(model_type, tp)
+        (hidden, tokens), (other_hidden, other_tokens) = self._inputs_with_others_replaced()
+
+        with torch.inference_mode(), InferenceMode.active():
+            try:
+                batched = self._draft(model, hidden, tokens)
+            except AssertionError as error:
+                if self.MLA_CACHED_LATENTS_ERROR not in str(error):
+                    raise
+                pytest.skip(
+                    "MLA with cached latents drafts without an inference context only with "
+                    "fix/n7-mla-mtp-draft"
+                )
+            # Every request but the last replaced: the last request's drafts must not move.
+            replaced = self._draft(model, other_hidden, other_tokens)
+            alone = self._draft_alone(model, hidden, tokens, monkeypatch)
+
+        self._assert_last_request_unmoved(batched, replaced)
+        for depth in range(self.MTP_DEPTHS):
+            # Different GEMM shapes and kernels round bf16 differently.
+            atol = 2e-2 * batched[depth].abs().max().item()
+            for i in range(self.NUM_REQUESTS):
+                torch.testing.assert_close(
+                    batched[depth][i],
+                    alone[i][depth][0],
+                    rtol=0,
+                    atol=atol,
+                    msg=lambda m: f"depth {depth}, request {i}: batched != alone\n{m}",
+                )
+
+    @pytest.mark.parametrize("model_type", ["gpt", "mla", "mamba", "gdp", "kda", "gdn2", "dsa_gqa"])
+    def test_graphed_draft_step(self, model_type):
+        """The draft steps capture into a CUDA graph, as the engine captures them, which needs
+        them to be free of host syncs. A replay drafts each request on its own, from the inputs
+        it is given."""
+        model = self._build_model(model_type, tp=1)
+        (hidden, tokens), (other_hidden, other_tokens) = self._inputs_with_others_replaced()
+        static_hidden, static_tokens = hidden.clone(), tokens.clone()
+
+        with torch.inference_mode(), InferenceMode.active():
+            eager = self._draft(model, hidden, tokens)
+            # Warm up on a side stream before capturing, so that Triton autotuning and library
+            # initialization stay out of the graph.
+            stream = torch.cuda.Stream()
+            stream.wait_stream(torch.cuda.current_stream())
+            with torch.cuda.stream(stream):
+                self._draft(model, static_hidden, static_tokens)
+            torch.cuda.current_stream().wait_stream(stream)
+            graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+            with torch.cuda.graph(graph):
+                graphed = self._draft(model, static_hidden, static_tokens)
+
+            graph.replay()
+            batched = [logits.clone() for logits in graphed]
+            static_hidden.copy_(other_hidden)
+            static_tokens.copy_(other_tokens)
+            graph.replay()
+            replaced = [logits.clone() for logits in graphed]
+
+        last = self.NUM_REQUESTS - 1
+        for depth in range(self.MTP_DEPTHS):
+            torch.testing.assert_close(
+                batched[depth],
+                eager[depth],
+                rtol=0,
+                atol=2e-2 * eager[depth].abs().max().item(),
+                msg=lambda m: f"depth {depth}: the replay differs from the eager draft\n{m}",
+            )
+            # The replay read the replaced inputs: every replaced request's drafts moved.
+            moved = (replaced[depth][:last] != batched[depth][:last]).any(dim=-1)
+            assert moved.all(), (
+                f"depth {depth}: replaying with replaced inputs left the drafts of requests "
+                f"{(~moved).nonzero().flatten().tolist()} unchanged"
+            )
+        self._assert_last_request_unmoved(batched, replaced)
